section: Occupational structure of India - trends and inter-state variation
subsections: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector
Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences
Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011
Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture

accepted.s: Which sector has consistently recorded the highest share of employment in India across the major workforce surveys mentioned?
accepted.x: Agriculture has remained the sector with the highest employment share, although its share has declined over time.
accepted.tq: Use the broad sector comparison and avoid the familiar but incorrect answer of cottage industries.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of workers engaged in agriculture in India was approximately what percentage in 1951?
accepted.x: Agriculture accounted for 72% of workers in 1951.
accepted.tq: Match the earliest year with the highest agricultural employment share.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following agricultural workforce shares in chronological order of the corresponding years:
A. 54.6%
B. 69.8%
C. 64.75%
D. 66.7%
accepted.tq: Arrange the figures by attaching each percentage to its year before ordering.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the decline in the agricultural share of workers from 1951 to 2011?
accepted.x: The agricultural share declined from 72% in 1951 to 54.6% in Census 2011.
accepted.tq: Compare the first and last values in the stated Census series.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of workers in agriculture recorded in the 1993-94 NSS was:
accepted.x: The NSS estimate for 1993-94 placed agriculture's share of workers at 64.75%.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced survey-year percentages.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the share of workers in agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. It was 58.2% in Census 2001.
2. It was 54.6% in Census 2011.
3. It was 46.1% according to PLFS 2023-24.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three figures are given for the respective Census or PLFS periods.
accepted.tq: Verify each percentage against its survey year instead of relying only on the direction of change.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2021-22, which of the following correctly gives the approximate shares of the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors in the workforce, respectively?
accepted.x: The 2021-22 workforce shares were primary 43.96%, secondary 22.24% and tertiary 33.80%.
accepted.tq: Read the sector order carefully; the figures are not arranged in ascending order.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of services in employment rose from 22.82% in 1993-94 to approximately what level in 2009-10?
accepted.x: Services' share increased from 22.82% in 1993-94 to 34.90% in 2009-10.
accepted.tq: Track the direction and magnitude of the sectoral shift using the two dated values.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the 1993-94 employment shares?
accepted.x: In 1993-94, agriculture accounted for 64.75%, industry 12.43% and services, including construction, 22.82%.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure agriculture figure and then verify the two smaller sector shares.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On the eve of Independence, the principal livelihood of the Indian population was:
accepted.x: Agriculture was the main livelihood on the eve of Independence.
accepted.tq: Test the historical baseline rather than the later structural trend.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the NSSO 70th round conducted in 2013, what proportion of rural households were agricultural households?
accepted.x: The NSSO 70th round reported that 57.8% of rural households were agricultural households.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a household percentage from workforce and sector-share percentages.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the workforce figures given for the recent PLFS estimates?
o: 61.6 crore in both PLFS 2025 and Q2 FY26
61.6 crore in PLFS 2025 and 56.2 crore employed in Q2 FY26
56.2 crore in PLFS 2025 and 61.6 crore employed in Q2 FY26
46.1 crore in PLFS 2025 and 56.2 crore employed in Q2 FY26
accepted.x: The workforce was reported as 61.6 crore in PLFS 2025, while 56.2 crore were employed in Q2 FY26.
accepted.tq: Separate the total workforce figure from the employed-person figure and their reference periods.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent employment shares:
1. Agriculture constituted 42.4% of total employment in PLFS Q2 FY26.
2. Services constituted 62.0% of urban employment in the same reference period.
3. Agriculture constituted 54.6% of total employment in PLFS Q2 FY26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Agriculture accounted for 42.4% of total employment and services for 62.0% of urban employment. The 54.6% figure belongs to Census 2011.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that transfers an older Census figure to a newer PLFS period.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the rural share of workers with the rural share of India's population in Census 2011?
accepted.x: Rural areas contained 72.4% of workers but 68.8% of the total population.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal of two similar rural percentages.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The total number of workers and the work participation rate reported for Census 2011 were approximately:
accepted.x: There were 48.19 crore workers and the work participation rate was 39.8%, implying about 60% non-workers.
accepted.tq: Keep the absolute number separate from the percentage rate.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approximate number of male workers reported in the Census 2011 workforce data was:
accepted.x: Male workers numbered approximately 332 million.
accepted.tq: Identify the gender-specific workforce figure rather than the cultivator or labourer counts.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the occupational distribution of female workers?
o: 55% were cultivators and 24% were salaried workers.
24% were agricultural labourers and 55% were cultivators.
55% were agricultural labourers and 24% were cultivators.
32.5% were agricultural labourers and 12.8% were cultivators.
accepted.x: Among female workers, 55% were agricultural labourers and 24% were cultivators.
accepted.tq: Separate the two female agricultural categories and avoid reversing their shares.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Women held only 12.8% of operational holdings. This fact is associated with which broader trend?
accepted.x: The low share of operational holdings held by women, alongside their agricultural work, is associated with the feminisation of agriculture.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical indicator with the concept it illustrates.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The female labour force participation rate for persons aged 15 years and above increased from 30% in 2019-20 to what level in 2025?
accepted.x: The female LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above rose from 30% to 40%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the overall female LFPR from the rural female LFPR.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the change in rural and urban female LFPR between 2019-20 and 2025?
accepted.x: Rural female LFPR rose from 33.0% to 45.9%, whereas urban female LFPR rose from 23.3% to 27.7%.
accepted.tq: Compare both geographic series without interchanging their starting and ending values.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about recent female employment:
1. Women constituted 32.5% of total employment in 2025.
2. Rural women accounted for 80% of the rise in female workers between 2017-18 and 2023-24.
3. Women constituted 50% of total employment in 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Women constituted 32.5% of employment, and rural women contributed 80% of the rise in female workers. The 50% claim is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Identify the false extreme share while retaining the two supported statements.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of rural women workers engaged in self-employment increased from 60% in 2011-12 to what percentage in 2023-24?
accepted.x: The self-employed share among rural women workers increased to 73% in 2023-24.
accepted.tq: Track the time-bound increase rather than confusing it with the overall self-employment share.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change in the overall quality composition of employment between the two PLFS reference points?
o: Regular wage or salaried employment fell from 24% to 22%, while self-employment rose from 56% to 58%.
Regular wage or salaried employment rose from 22% to 24%, while self-employment fell from 58% to 56%.
Both regular wage employment and self-employment rose by 2 percentage points.
Both regular wage employment and self-employment fell by 2 percentage points.
accepted.x: The regular wage or salaried share rose from 22% to 24%, whereas self-employment declined from 58% to 56%.
accepted.tq: Use the opposite movement of the two employment categories as the key discriminator.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Women earned what proportion of men's wages in the three categories of salaried, casual and self-employed work, respectively?
accepted.x: Women's earnings were 76% of men's wages in salaried work, 69% in casual work and 36% in self-employment.
accepted.tq: Maintain the order of the employment categories while matching the wage ratios.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of women in salaried jobs increased from 16.6% in 2024 to what percentage in 2025?
accepted.x: Women's share in salaried jobs rose from 16.6% to 18.2%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the salaried-job share from the overall female employment share.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What proportion of women outside the labour force reportedly cited caregiving as the reason?
accepted.x: Approximately 40-44% of women outside the labour force cited caregiving responsibilities.
accepted.tq: Identify the range associated with the reason for non-participation, not an employment category.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a factor driving the feminisation of agriculture?
o: Rapid expansion of formal manufacturing jobs
accepted.x: Subsistence farming, unpaid family work and distress employment were identified as drivers. Rapid expansion of formal manufacturing jobs was not identified as a driver.
accepted.tq: Find the option that contradicts the stated explanation for feminisation of agriculture.
accepted.sec: Rural vs urban workforce (Census 2011), gender differences  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Between 2001 and 2011, which change occurred in the number of cultivators and agricultural labourers?
o: Cultivators increased and agricultural labourers decreased.
Cultivators decreased and agricultural labourers increased.
Both cultivators and agricultural labourers increased.
Both cultivators and agricultural labourers decreased.
accepted.x: Cultivators declined from 127.3 million to 118.8 million, while agricultural labourers increased from 106.8 million to 144.3 million.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of change in the two closely related occupational categories.
accepted.sec: Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Census 2011, agricultural labourers and cultivators constituted what shares of workers, respectively?
accepted.x: Agricultural labourers constituted 30.0% of workers, while cultivators constituted 24.7%.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two occupational shares in the comparison.
accepted.sec: Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The number of agricultural labourers first exceeded the number of cultivators in which Census?
accepted.x: In 2011, agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators for the first time.
accepted.tq: Use the milestone year rather than the year in which the underlying trend began.
accepted.sec: Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the reduction in the number of cultivators between 2001 and 2011?
o: Fragmentation of holdings and the increasing share of small and marginal farmers
Exclusive movement of all workers into services
accepted.x: Fragmentation reduced the average holding size and increased the relative importance of small and marginal farmers, contributing to the decline in cultivators.
accepted.tq: Link the occupational trend to the structural cause rather than an absolute claim about sectoral movement.
accepted.sec: Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The average size of an operational holding declined from 2.28 hectares in 1971 to what level in 2015-16?
accepted.x: The average holding size fell to 1.08 hectares in 2015-16 from 2.28 hectares in 1971.
accepted.tq: Read the temporal direction of the landholding change carefully.
accepted.sec: Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Small and marginal farmers accounted for approximately what share of farmers?
accepted.x: Small and marginal farmers constituted approximately 86% of farmers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the farmer-size composition figure from rural workforce percentages.
accepted.sec: Trend shifts - cultivators vs agricultural labourers, Census 2001 to 2011  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Occupational structure refers to the:
o: Distribution of workforce across primary, secondary and tertiary activities
Distribution of land among cultivators and labourers
Distribution of population only among rural and urban areas
Share of national income received by different occupations
accepted.x: Occupational structure is the distribution of the workforce across primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
accepted.tq: Select the exact definition and distinguish workforce distribution from income or land distribution.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: As an economy develops, occupational structure generally tends to shift away from:
accepted.x: Economic development is generally associated with a shift of workers away from farming towards secondary and tertiary activities.
accepted.tq: Apply the standard structural-transformation relationship.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a reason identified for the slow movement of Indian workers out of agriculture?
o: Manufacturing's limited absorption of farm labour
Abundant formal vocational training for almost all workers
accepted.x: Only 4.2% had formal vocational training, so abundant formal vocational training is not a reason for the slow shift.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that reverses the stated skills constraint.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: The employment share of agriculture fell only marginally during the Plan era mainly because of:
o: The universal availability of formal non-farm jobs
A complete shift to capital-intensive manufacturing
accepted.x: Population pressure on land helped keep a large workforce dependent on agriculture, so its employment share declined only marginally during the Plan era.
accepted.tq: Connect the demographic pressure with the persistence of agricultural employment.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the relationship between services-led growth and occupational transformation in India?
o: Services-led growth automatically absorbs all agricultural labour regardless of skills.
Services-led growth causes agriculture's employment share to rise in every period.
Services-led growth eliminates the need for manufacturing employment.
Services-led growth requires skills, limiting the movement of workers without appropriate capabilities.
accepted.x: Services-led growth needs appropriate skills, which limits the absorption of surplus agricultural labour into service-sector employment.
accepted.tq: Identify the qualification attached to the otherwise positive effect of services-led growth.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: The failure of manufacturing to absorb sufficient farm labour is described as:
accepted.x: The limited absorption of farm labour by manufacturing is associated with premature deindustrialisation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the structural-development term and related labour-market concepts.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: Capital-intensive growth may slow the shift out of agriculture because it:
o: Creates large numbers of formal non-farm jobs with little investment.
Raises the number of small agricultural holdings directly.
Fails to absorb surplus agricultural labour into formal non-farm jobs.
accepted.x: Capital-intensive growth may fail to absorb surplus agricultural labour into formal non-farm employment.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that states the employment consequence rather than an unrelated effect of capital intensity.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: Only what proportion of workers had formal vocational training according to the cited PLFS figure?
accepted.x: Only 4.2% had formal vocational training.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the vocational-training percentage from employment-quality percentages.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which numerical comparison illustrates the imbalance between new labour-market entrants and new jobs?
o: About 20 million entrants and 2 million new jobs annually
About 2 million entrants and 20 million new jobs annually
About 4.2 million entrants and 2 million new jobs annually
About 20 million entrants and 20 million new jobs annually
accepted.x: Approximately 20 million people enter the labour market annually, compared with only about 2 million new jobs and few formal employers.
accepted.tq: Compare the two annual flows and watch for their reversal.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: Colonial deindustrialisation contributed to the persistence of agricultural employment because it:
o: Increased the average size of holdings
accepted.x: Colonial deindustrialisation had already pushed artisans onto the land, increasing pressure on agriculture.
accepted.tq: Match the historical process with its stated labour-market consequence.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - meaning, and reasons for the slow shift out of agriculture  [other exams]

accepted.s: In the latest quarter cited, the share of rural agricultural employment fell from 58.5% to:
accepted.x: Rural agricultural employment declined from 58.5% to 55.8% in January-March 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the latest rural trend from the all-India and urban sector figures.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the latest quarter cited, the shares of rural secondary and tertiary employment were approximately:
accepted.x: Rural secondary employment accounted for 22.6% and tertiary employment for 21.7%.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of the two non-agricultural sectors in the latest-quarter comparison.
accepted.sec: Occupational structure - share of workforce by sector (Census, NSS, PLFS), highest-employment sector  [APPSC]
